Documents from the US Department of Justice, consisting of both emails and photos, testify to close contacts between Epstein and the British heavyweight.  That Mandelson appears in the picture in old white underpants in Epstein's apartment in Paris is in this context a minor detail; significantly more serious is that he shared market-sensitive information and gave Epstein insight behind the scenes into London's political top echelons, including during the coalition negotiations in 2010.

From Berlin to Dresden by high-speed train In the south of Berlin, a new railway line shines in the sun. Double tracks, high noise barriers and a nail-straight stretch to the south. It is Germany's newest high-speed line, which opened at the beginning of December 2025 and makes the journey between Berlin and Dresden ten minutes faster. The project took 20 years to plan and seven years to build – but without any delays. The next step is to extend the route to the Czech capital Prague. Then the travel time between Berlin and Prague will be reduced to two and a half hours, compared to almost five hours today. Such a project is exactly what the European Commission wants the member states to invest in. Underinvestment, cheap tickets and short-term thinking But according to Christian Böttger, it will take years before a similar project can be inaugurated in Germany – or in Europe as a whole. According to him, billions are missing to even renovate the existing railway. The funds that do exist are often used for short-term solutions or for politically popular measures, such as lowering the price of train tickets. In Germany, years of underinvestment are clearly visible. Only about 62 percent of the trains run on time. Sweden is average within the EU, but still manages better, with around 87 percent on time. - In such a situation, to believe that new high-speed lines will be built within 15 years is wishful thinking, he says.

Must listen more to the children The authority has several proposals for measures that must be presented to the government. An important part is more collaboration. - We can see in retrospect that the police had certain duties, the social service had certain duties and the health care service others. But putting the puzzle together and assessing risks in a structured way - that has been missing in these cases, says Moa Mannheimer. Another measure identified is that the child's situation must be strengthened. - You need to listen more to the children's voice both within healthcare, the police and social services. Among the guinea pigs was "Grandma Rosiepuff", the oldest guinea pig who is believed to be the mother of many of the others. - She is probably related to all of them. At the same time, care is taken to only place the guinea pig with serious animal owners.  - We do not sell small animals to be kept in cages. We do not sell small animals to be toys for children, of course. So we look for the perfect homes.  Guinea pigs can live between five and ten years if cared for properly. They need large areas to move around, such as a paddock or their own room, and should never be kept alone. They require companionship, a proper diet of fresh vegetables and free access to hay.

Especially high pressure and freezing temperatures go hand in hand during the winter months, not least when it becomes prolonged.  In meteorology, such a locked-in high pressure is called a high-pressure blockage, and is what lays the foundation for weather extremes. - Blocking high pressure creates winter's cold snaps and summer's heat waves, explains TV4 meteorologist Ulrika Elvgren. Therefore the cold remains The reason why the high pressure has become permanent is partly that it consists of slowly sinking air, that is to say that it receives its air supply from above. The cold air is also heavier than the warm, and air accumulation (high pressure) therefore thrives in the atmosphere closest to the ground. In order to break the high-pressure bucket, an extensive low pressure with a substantial portion of mild air is therefore required.  But during periods of high pressure blocking, the low pressure is instead guided around the high pressure and the cold, as now, is allowed to remain undisturbed.  - It's a locked-in weather situation and we've had this high pressure now for several weeks, but it might start to weaken a little during the next week and let in a little more weakened frontal zones, says Ulrika Elvgren. - We have already received a little more snow in southern Sweden. But it looks like the cold air won't let go. A cold domain lies over the whole of northern Europe and into the Russian continent and further east, she adds. "No clear mild air coming in" Although the high pressure may change at the beginning of next week, one should not count on the cold air to disappear because of it. Further ahead, the forecasts are too uncertain to be able to draw any conclusions. - It looks like colder air will return as we approach the middle of February. We have no clear mild air coming in. The gray space rock, which weighs over 2.5 tons, was discovered during a routine inspection of a sea container in the port of St. Petersburg. A criminal investigation has now been opened by prosecutors. The Aletai meteorite was discovered in western China back in 1898 and is estimated to be at least 4.5 billion years old – almost as old as the solar system itself.  Scientists have long warned about the growing trade in meteorites, which are often invaluable to research and can provide important clues about the early history of the solar system.

Part-time work is a factor that affects the long term. If you work part-time for more than four years when the children are small, it can start to be felt in the pension. During the first four years, there is pension entitlement for childhood years in the general pension system, which largely compensates for the loss of income. The reason behind the fatal accidents can be several, and the snow-poor winter that prevails in large parts of the Alps is likely one of them. Less snow means that the snow is less compacted, and in addition weak layers of snow can remain for several weeks. - They are difficult for the common man to follow - and also for professionals, says Petter Palmgren, avalanche expert at the Swedish Environmental Protection Agency. A catalyst for accidents In addition to weather, a large proportion of accidents can be explained by the human factor. The majority of avalanches that occur are triggered naturally, but the avalanches that lead to deaths are almost exclusively triggered by humans, says Petter Palmgren. Statistically, accidents increase the more people are in the ski systems, and therefore the combination of newly fallen snow and snow-poor winters is a bit of a catalyst for accidents. - When a little snow finally falls, many people are starved for good skiing. Large avalanches are then quite common. Until the beginning of February in the previous two seasons, a total of 28 and 30 people respectively lost their lives in avalanche accidents in the Alps, according to figures from EAWS. This year, there have thus been almost twice as many fatal accidents within the same time period. - It's probably quite a lot for the time of year, says Petter Palmgren. Residents of the region are 15 times more likely to die in the war than residents of Moscow. - Calm in the capitals and the North Caucasus has traditionally been very important for maintaining social order and stability in Russia, says Alexander Kolyandr. In some of Russia's poorest regions – Chechnya, Ingushetia and Karachay-Cherkessia – deaths per capita are on a par with the rich cities of Moscow and Saint Petersburg. Sent to the front instead of trial Over half of all dead are voluntary, mobilized or convicted criminals from correctional facilities. People who had no connection to the army before the outbreak of war. Defendants in criminal cases have fallen among the dead, compared to a year ago.

4923a8cb079c5d82c51dd339f02e7ebe2f5d8cba: Tried to mislabel expired candy - five tons seized
402332fe1356aa00d70d52264090d5dab646d6ea: When Malmö city inspectors recently visited a wholesale company, 5.2 tons of approximately one-year-old candy were discovered that were about to be relabeled with new best-before dates. This is reported by the news agency Siren. Two people who were working on packaging goods in connection with ten pallets of candy boxes immediately left the premises when the inspectors showed up, according to the environmental administration.  - We are doing outreach to inventory premises, including in this area, which is densely packed with wholesalers. When two people stick out immediately when we arrive, it of course arouses our interest, says unit manager Caroline Tandefelt to Nyhetsbyrån Siren. On a follow-up visit, those in charge stated that the candy had accidentally not been disposed of. "In the premises there were prepared packing surfaces, empty new cartons, unused bags for repackaging, tape, sealing machine and solvents in the form of acetone and nail polish remover with the aim of removing labels and erasing the best before date", writes the environmental administration in its decision. Cat chasing mice The spaces in the premises were also dirty and unhygienic. Among other things, a cat had been placed there to keep mice and vermin away. "There was a litter box in the toilet and cat food was stored in the fridge," the decision states. In recent years, the wholesale company has been the subject of several controls and banning decisions.  Contact with Danish colleagues The delivery in question, which according to the environmental administration had come from the Netherlands, is still taped up in the premises and is to be destroyed under the supervision of the municipality - We have also been in contact with our Danish colleagues on the other side of the strait. It is about a very large volume, and overall the data we have indicates a certain systematicity, says Caroline Tandefelt to News Agency Siren. The property where the environmental administration's raid took place is owned by another company with partly the same group of owners. Several wholesale companies in the food industry have their warehouses nearby.
30a5831fe67213b9a31432f9080572301030c44f: Livia went for the bench press record - then she broke both arms
bc93af5c72c807b977b09509cb2ee6ef7d4a655c: The accident occurred during the bench press WC in Eskilstuna on January 25. After lifting 170 kilos, Livia Blomqvist, 23, tried to break the Nordic record of 178 kilos. During the lift, she heard a crack - and then another - as the bar ended up at the wrong angle and both arms broke. - Then it felt like in that second the dream of the World Cup came crashing down, says Livia Blomqvist in Nyhetsmorgon.  "The second time in my life I've heard of this" Blomqvist competed in the so-called equipped bench press, a technical branch where everything has to be right. She says that her shoulder blades gave way, causing the bar to go backwards towards her head. The arm ended up at such a bad angle that the leg came off and she lost control of the bar - then the other arm came off too.  Chief physician Mikael Sandström states that it is very unusual for athletes to break both arms at the same time. - It is the second time in my life I have heard about this, says Sandström. Despite the injury, Blomqvist managed to qualify for both the WC and EC, but now awaits a long rehabilitation.  - I try to maintain my body as much as possible and hope to be able to train lighter weights as soon as possible, she says. Tough way back Despite the setback, Blomqvist is determined to get back to the competition scene. She continues to train what she can and hopes that the injury may even give her body time to heal old wear and tear. - If only I can train 40 kilos in the bench press, it will do a lot for my strength, says Blomqvist. The doctors have prescribed at least twelve weeks of rest from heavy load, which makes the WC in May unlikely. Blomqvist is now aiming to be back at the EC in August. - You'll see how the body responds, but I've made up my mind that the EC in August is a more realistic goal.

However, the change does not apply to rules for emissions from power plants and other stationary sources, such as oil and gas facilities. But overturning the original decision could pave the way for those rules to be dismantled as well, writes The Wall Street Journal. 7fb2a5a4ce2abc2fdff2a22d38417a80d2e378eb: CIA manual from World War II goes viral in the US
c37de03fc58e55c3246925a74de56a370dddb21a: The text was written during World War II by William "Wild Bill" Donovan, head of the Office of Strategic Services which later became the CIA. The manual was published in 2008. In the last month, it has been downloaded nearly 60,000 times and is now the fifth most popular e-book on Project Gutenberg, an American literature project that works to make available literature that is not covered by copyright. Small actions slow down the system The manual describes so-called "simple sabotage". It is about everyday behaviors that, if repeated, can make it difficult for a bureaucracy to function. Among the advice is to: Give long speeches and drag out meetings.  Bring up side issues and discuss details unnecessarily.  "Misunderstanding" instructions, asking many questions and delaying answers. It is also suggested to play dumb, be as annoying and argumentative as possible without breaking rules, as well as to stop talking when representatives of the regime enter a room. The purpose, according to the authors, is to make the work of the police and security services more difficult, but also to give ordinary people a way to show resistance to decisions they perceive as unacceptable. Attention in today's USA Why the manual has gone viral right now is unclear. According to the online newspaper 404 Media, the interest coincides with a period of unrest and change in the American workplace, especially among government employees. Questions of loyalty, reorganizations and new demands on employees have become more common in a more polarized political climate. During Donald Trump's time in power, discussions about the role of the state and the independence of the authorities have again taken place in the public debate. In that context, the old CIA manual has received new attention among some readers. On a large online forum for government employees, one of the most-read posts is headlined: "To my colleagues, especially veterans: we are at war." There, the manual is shared primarily as a historical document – ​​and as a basis for discussion.

- The booking situation looks good and it is true. But the notes are smaller. Many restaurateurs testify to that, says Peder Dinkelspiel.

Lova Vesterlund was only two months old when the childcare center noticed that she was not gaining weight. The family was sent to Gävle hospital and after several examinations it was clear that she had a serious congenital heart defect.  - It was terrible. It felt like someone pulled something from under our feet, says Ingela Eriksson, Lova's mother.  For large parts of her life, Lova has been cared for in hospital, and got to meet many hospital clowns, she says in Nyhetsmorgon. In total, she has been operated on four times, with the first operation taking almost twelve hours. Today she has both a pacemaker and a mechanical valve.  - Now I have a pacemaker up here, says Lova and points to her chest.  In 2024, seven children died Despite her congenital heart defect, Lova lives an active life and moves like any seven-year-old – she climbs, plays and is constantly in motion.  - We usually say that she is more wild than tame and joke that it is her pacemaker that is an extra battery and drives her to keep going, says Ingela Eriksson.  Every year around 2,000 children are born in Sweden with congenital heart defects. According to Kristina Sparreljung, secretary general of the Heart-Lung Foundation, survival has improved greatly in recent decades. In 2000, 39 children with congenital heart defects died. In 2024, the number was seven. - This development has been driven by the technological development that made it possible to find children with severe congenital heart defects already during pregnancy. This means that these children can be received in prepared operating units, says Kristina Sparreljung. "Live now, die later" She states that research has progressed, among other things through the possibility today to see children's hearts in three-dimensional images - something that was not possible just a few years ago. At the same time, there are continuing challenges. 

- Children with congenital heart defects suffer to a greater extent than other adults from other cardiovascular complications earlier in life, says Kristina Sparreljung.  Lova likes to take her medicine with a little vanilla ice cream

The study is based on a survey of 2,000 families in Gaza, selected to represent the population. The researchers tallied both direct and indirect deaths between the terrorist attack on Israel on October 7, 2023 and January 5, 2025. In total, 42,200 women, children and the elderly died in attacks – 56 percent of the direct deaths. The study also shows that the Ministry of Health's reporting on the proportion of women, children and the elderly among the dead has been correct. Fewer indirect deaths The researchers estimate that 3-4 percent of Gaza's population has been killed in the conflict. A further 8,000 people are believed to have died indirectly from, for example, diseases or malnutrition, according to the study.  Researcher Michael Spagat has been working on calculating deaths in conflicts for twenty years.  He questions an earlier study, also published in the Lancet, which showed that the indirect deaths were far more than the direct ones – probably around four times as many.  - In Gaza, there were initially resources in the form of trained doctors and a functioning health system. In addition, the area is small, so once help arrives it can be quickly distributed, says Spagat. May never get answers Data on death tolls have been disputed. An Israeli security source recently said the Gaza health ministry's figures are "largely correct". The Department of Health now states that over 71,660 people have been killed directly by Israeli attacks, including more than 570 after the October 2025 ceasefire. Other studies have reached similar conclusions, but some have estimated even more indirect deaths and a greatly reduced life expectancy. The researchers behind the Lancet study believe that it will take a long time before there is a complete picture of the death toll.

- It is not a given that there will be a large research project to reconstruct what actually happened. It will take a long time before we get a full account of all the dead in Gaza, if we ever get it, says Michael Spagat.

On December 3, 2024, the then president of South Korea gave an unexpected televised speech in which he pointed to threats from North Korea and "anti-state forces".  He declared a state of military emergency, the country's first in four decades, and ordered the military to surround parliament.  Dramatic images of politicians barricading themselves in the parliament building, soldiers trying to storm it and civilians trying to stop armored vehicles were shared around the world.  Six hours The decision was made without political support and within six hours the National Assembly managed to gather and vote to overturn it. The state of emergency lasted for six hours.  The incident sparked mass protests and was described as an attempt to condone Yoon's power.  Ten days later, parliament voted to impeach him. He was immediately suspended and later formally deposed as well. Long investigation The investigation against the former president continued throughout 2025. Yoon has defended his decisions as necessary to protect democracy. Prosecutors have argued throughout that the president abused his power to neutralize political opponents and circumvent the democratic process.  Yesterday he was sentenced by the court in Seoul to life imprisonment for attempted sedition.  Judge Ji Gwi-yeon found that Yoon sent troops to the National Assembly to silence political opponents who opposed his government.  
- The court finds that the intention was to paralyze the congregation for a considerable period of time, he says. eecab15f6a8c114cd86126619560b63740a44fae: The Delsjö area in Gothenburg is used as the city's raw water reservoir and water is pumped both in and out of the lakes. After weeks of freezing temperatures, the bodies of water are covered by a solid layer of ice, but appearances can be deceiving. Although the ice looks stable, these types of lakes where the water is regulated can be treacherous. - When the water level changes, the ice becomes weaker. It breaks up. Cracks can appear in the ice and therefore the ice can become dangerous, says Anton El Raai, operating engineer for circulation and water within the City of Gothenburg. Like a hammock In Gothenburg, the municipality has specifically warned against entering the Delsjöarna, but this type of regulated lakes can be found all over the country. It is not enough that the ice itself becomes unstable. If water is drained after the ice has formed, a gap of several decimetres can be created between the ice cover and the water surface. - Then it becomes even more dangerous, because then the ice becomes like a hammock above the water and then you can fall if you feel bad, says Kim Loob Almbratt, biologist at Sportfiskarna. This "hammock effect" on the one hand increases the pressure on the ice when the water does not relieve it, and on the other hand the person who falls through risks getting stuck under the ice without the possibility of climbing up. The expert advises against When TV4 meets Kim Loob Almbratt, he and Sportfiskarna are out with a school class showing things you can do on the ice, such as ice fishing. But they are not out on the Delsjöarna, but have chosen another lake in Gothenburg where the ice is stable. - I wouldn't have ventured out on an ice that has a lot of regulation, nor a water source if I'm not absolutely sure that I will be able to handle this. I don't think common people should go out on regulated lakes, says Kim Loob Almbratt.

Despite the dramatic name, blood rain is therefore harmless - and not entirely unusual either. It happens once a year and is most common on the west coast.

5f9f025f34082346b652e4bd1aec53f36a7f63b0: Screen eyes is often called digital eye fatigue and means tired, dry and irritated eyes caused by screen work. Symptoms can be headache, blurred vision and neck pain. It occurs, among other things, because we blink less often. - It is important to have the screen at the right height. If you have the screen a little too high, you are forced to stare more and blink too little. You are so interested in focusing on what you are doing that you blink less, says Bo Andersén. Ergonomics and breaks Sitting correctly and ergonomically is therefore part of the solution. - When you are interested, you like to curl up. You should sit ergonomically, with your shoulders back. Like being out riding. Sway in the back and the screen at the right distance, says Bo Andersén in Nyhetsmorgon. Another important point is to take breaks. There is something called the 20-20-20 rule and it means that every 20 minutes you rest your eyes for 20 seconds on something that is 20 feet (about 6 meters) away. The eyes change with age. For problems with dry, itchy eyes, Andersén recommends starting with terminal glasses in time. So-called presbyopia, or presbyopia, usually occurs at the age of 45 and also affects the eyes. - Then maybe an eye examination is even needed. Some struggle up to 55, but then they probably have a bit more headaches and discomfort, says Bo Andersén. With age, the production of lubricant in the glands in the eyes also decreases. Then you may need eye drops. Then you should examine yourself. Another everyday problem is small things that move around in the eye or in the field of vision, so-called vitreous detachment. It is a harmless age-related change in which the eye's jelly detaches from the retina. - It is extremely common. It's a little scary and you get a little worried, but I usually compare it to the skin wrinkling. You can have small figures in the field of vision and the typical thing is that it follows the movements, says Andersén. Word of the bug quickly spread on social media and players rushed to the platform. Now ATG collects money from players in district courts and via the Kronofogden, after the so-called "bug day".  - We had a technical problem which meant that customers could withdraw money they were not entitled to. Quite quickly we fixed it, shut down the error, and then we ended up in the situation we are in now, says Jan Sonnevi.  In the last month alone, the company has won or settled over 20 civil cases linked to the incident. - They got several chances to pay. We sent reminders, but in the end we had to send them on to the Norwegian Kronofogdemyndigheten, says Jan Sonnevi, casino manager at ATG.  In total, ATG has upwards of 300 claim cases in court from last year and this year, although it is not confirmed that all of them concern the bug.  Turnover increased fivefold On May 16, ATG sent refunds to players who received winnings paid out without coverage. According to reports that TV4 has seen, the turnover on that day was fivefold compared to a normal day. The same judgments also show that the number of new players was 24 times higher. - They know what they are doing, it is money they are not entitled to, but they try to take it anyway, says Julia Axelsson, contract law lawyer.  Hope for a solution There are still a large number of claims that have not yet gone to court. Exactly when the process is over is difficult to say. - We of course hope that it will be resolved as soon as possible. We have no intention or desire to pursue a process against our customers, we want to move on, so I hope it ends as soon as possible, says Jan Sonnevi.

Relabeling prohibited Marie-Louise Danielsson-Tham, professor of food hygiene, explains that it is forbidden to change the best-before date on food.
- It is forbidden to relabel a product with a longer shelf life, she says.

At the same time, she says that it is not illegal to sell goods where the best before date has passed, as long as it is done with the original label. - In that case, I would recommend that they had sold these with the original markings. But on the other hand, who would want to buy 16 year old corn balls? How to detect old snacks How do you know if the snacks are too old?
- Of course you taste them. The first thing that usually happens is that they go rancid, explains Danielsson-Tham. She also advises to pay attention to packaging where labels are pasted on top of the original labelling.
- If you see that something is stuck on a package, then you should be suspicious and ask the store what it is about. Snacks can last for several months According to Danielsson-Tham, it is difficult to say exactly how long snacks such as cheese balls and corn balls last, but they are often edible several months after the best before date if the bag is well sealed. - Months after the best-before date, they should be edible, she says.

But it is not only in the winter that she is affected, says Camilla Jensen. She can feel it even when it's hot, if the weather changes. - It can be 30 degrees outside, but when it starts to wind or rain, I immediately feel that my fingers are getting cold. If I've worked out, I have to change within five minutes. According to 1177, it is unknown what causes the phenomenon, but there is a certain heredity. If you work a lot with machines that vibrate, have a high stress level or have some other illness, it can lead to Raynaud's syndrome. Pain when sensation returns Camilla Jensen has tried tricks like electric gloves and hand warmers to no avail, and dresses as much as she can. - People think I'm going on a polar expedition, then they panic when they see my fingers. Researchers from the UK, Canada and Denmark analyzed sperm samples from 15,581 men in Denmark and Florida aged 18 to 45 between 2018-2024. The aim has been to investigate which factors affect the movement speed of the sperm - an important aspect in fertility investigations.  - This is a study that can give us a little more knowledge about how we can work with infertility and involuntary childlessness, which we see that the World Health Organization (WHO) claims is an increasingly common problem, says Kalle Norwald, psychotherapist and sexologist who has taken part in the study. Faster sperm in June and July The results show that sperm swim faster during June and July, both in Denmark and Florida. But the researchers could not see that it was the outdoor temperature that was behind the difference. 

- It is rather about us moving more during the summer months, says Norwald. Sperm had the lowest ability during the colder months, December to January. This despite climatic and demographic differences. Lifestyle an important factor According to Norwald, it is likely that lifestyle factors such as increased physical activity, more time outdoors and reduced stress during the holidays play a major role in sperm quality.  - When you have involuntary childlessness or it takes a long time to get pregnant, you need to pull all the strings. If you tried during the winter months without results, this could be part of the explanation, says Kalle Norwald.  Several factors affect fertility Norwald points out that sperm speed is only one of many factors that affect fertility. - It is actually only 50 percent of an embryo, a future fetus that then becomes a child. So this study really only shows the sperm cells and nothing on the egg cells but it could be a part. The study's conclusion shows that understanding these seasonal patterns could improve fertility treatments by optimizing the timing of treatment. It would also provide better guidance to couples trying to conceive.

He particularly highlights deportations of migrant workers and their children. - We have had different types of legislation that have made it possible to get here. Partly a very free labor immigration that came in 2008. Alongside that, the change of track, that those who apply for asylum in Sweden but are refused, have the opportunity to change to a work permit. These people have been given a promise and the politicians have been clear that we want people to come here and work in Swedish companies. That legislation has since been scrapped without transitional provisions enabling them to remain.

Kopsch has partly traveled around the country and met people who are to be deported, partly he has also made videos on social media about people in the same situation. Thus was born the book itself, where these cases are highlighted. "Of course people get pissed off" In the book, Kopsch proposes a so-called establishment amnesty, where the track changers should be able to get a permanent residence permit. He believes that it was never intended that this group would be affected by the new rules. 

- These are people we want to keep in Sweden. Of course we will not deport them. It's very bad for the Swedish economy and we won't be able to manage healthcare if we deport them, says Kopsch. 

He says he understands the outrage people have when teenage deportations happen. - Politicians say: We must deport murderers and rapists, then you read in the newspaper that here we have a rapist whom we should not deport. The same day you read: Here we have an 18-year-old girl with good high school grades and a Swedish boyfriend, we are going to deport her. It's clear that people get pissed off when you read things like that. "Never been easy to vote" Kopsch also criticizes the political rhetoric around the migration issue. He believes that the term "strict migration policy" has been misinterpreted. – P

Angelica Bengtsson has been unemployed since she graduated a year and a half ago.

And it is precisely in several Scanian municipalities that have the highest percentages of young people aged 18 to 24 registered with the Employment Service. For example Bromölla, Åstorp and Östra Göinge. In the main town of Broby in Östra Göinge, the municipality started Göingematchningen, a kind of municipal employment agency, after the Employment Agency closed its local office.

- It works great, I've worked here for five years and it's always been busy, especially when we have themes and companies here, there's often a bit of a queue because everyone wants to fight for the jobs, says Camilla Larsson. Jobs are created in the big cities The reason why youth unemployment is so high in smaller municipalities that used to have industries is because most of the jobs that are created today take place in the big cities.

- This means that labor is laid off in these locations and they find it difficult to find new jobs. Sweden's labor market is quite good for those with a good education and high qualifications, but we lack jobs where you can take a slightly lower education and quite quickly find a way to support yourself, says Andreas Bergh, docent in economics at Lund University.

On the other hand, the high youth unemployment rate overall may be due to students looking for jobs, according to him.

- It can be a good sign that you make contacts in the labor market early on and perhaps treat yourself to being a little picky about which jobs you take. But it can also be the case that people are looking for a job because they find it difficult to find a job. Then of course it's problematic because then it's a sign that it's difficult to get in when you're new to the labor market, says Andreas Bergh.

f997218ad79b7d4a1d694281460d3ce011218335:
February was characterized by a stability in food prices overall, but behind the numbers there are both sharp increases and decreases. Beef and ground beef have become much more expensive – in one year, prices have risen by almost 30 percent, mainly due to meat shortages. A tenth cheaper juice Even berries, especially lingonberries and blueberries, have continued to rise in price. At the same time, certain vegetables, such as eggplant and zucchini, as well as juice and fruit drinks have become significantly cheaper. - We drink less juice and there is a bigger selection now so it is going downhill. A two-liter is almost a tenth cheaper. There are big changes there, says Ulf Mazur. Ahead of the impending reduction in food VAT, Matpriskollen has noticed a record-breaking commitment from consumers. Many get in touch and suspect stealth increases, but according to Mazur, it is often about natural price movements in a large and complex industry. - You are so burned by all the price increases that have been, he says and continues: - But it is that we also see that some chains are really resisting price increases now. Maybe they will come later instead, says Ulf Mazur. This means the VAT reduction From 1 April, the VAT on food will be reduced from 12 to 6 percent. But the price reduction will not be exactly 6 percent, but 5.36 percent, because VAT is a tax on the price the store sets.

The reduction only applies to food – not pet food, shampoo, detergents, medicines or tobacco. In addition, intensive work is underway in the industry to ensure that all prices are correctly marked before the transition, which takes place in the middle of Easter week. - It is a huge challenge. You probably won't have time to notice all the shelf edges, but on the other hand, the checkout price must be the right one, says Ulf Mazur.

Clear, measurable disturbances in the body's regulation of pulse and blood pressure have been seen.  In some there are signs of influence in the small autonomic nerve fibers. But many have already received notice of the tax - from fraudsters. "Your tax refund has been approved. In order to complete the process and receive your tax refund, you need to verify your bank details and confirm your identity via our secure system," reads a fraud attempt that the Internet Foundation has seen. - There have been scam emails like this about refunds ever since December, says Björn Appelgren. Some emails prompt the recipient to scan a QR code. - It is a slightly newer version that often leads to a site that looks exactly like the Tax Agency's. On the site there is a form where you have to fill in your payment card details and with that information the fraudsters can hijack your card and use it. Empty the account It also happens that fraudsters call. - In telephone scams, it is common for them to try to get you to use your bank ID incorrectly so that they can empty your accounts, says Appelgren.  Sometimes they try to install a virus program. This is often done via an email with an attached file where, for example, it may say "declaration notice" or "error report declaration". If you download the file, things can go wrong. - Then you infect your computer with some form of spyware that can lie in the background and steal valuable information from us. Do not open The Internet Foundation's tip to avoid being scammed is to never click on links or scan QR codes in messages from senders claiming to be the Swedish Tax Agency. You should also not open or download attached files. - The Swedish Tax Agency will never contact you via email or SMS in matters where you need to share payment card details. The declaration and communication about it are sent via your digital mailbox or as physical mail. Another tip is to contact the authority yourself if you feel unsure. - You look up a contact route yourself or log in via their e-service.

702c7dc99032b8082e931cc2105fde4da80823cb: The idea emerged when municipal politician Elmer Eriksson (M) reacted to how much working time is spent on meetings where few or no decisions are made. There are around 15,000 employees in Umeå municipality and, according to Eriksson, around 17 percent of working time is spent on meetings. He estimates that even a small reduction in meeting time could free up large sums. - In round numbers, it could be almost SEK 220 million. That money could be spent on the seniors or school students instead, he says in a proposal that was first raised in a submission in the Västerbottens-Kuriren. Want to make the cost visible In order to get more people to think about it, Eriksson wants the cost to be visible already when a meeting is booked. In the system, the number of participants and the length of the meeting must be automatically converted into money. - Then a price picture should come up immediately that tells you how much the meeting costs. Then you get food for thought, he says. The hope is that fewer people will be called to meetings and that the meetings that are held will be shorter and more focused. - Maybe next time you should take fewer people who are not really needed, or make sure that the meeting goes faster. Large meetings can be expensive According to Eriksson, large meetings with many participants can quickly add up in costs. He estimates that each working hour per person costs around SEK 500, including social security contributions. - Then you realize what the meeting actually costs. Maybe next time they should bring fewer people, or talk faster. He emphasizes that the proposal is not about stopping necessary meetings, but about using the municipality's resources more efficiently. - You can be a little tighter both in number of people and in time, and spend the money on the residents, says Elmer Eriksson.

bc253ba8daca5fdfaca0aef8d3d30f6bfc3276d8: The dietitian's trick: How to get children to eat vegetables
031930a471d6d456796273f7a604ab900ee536a1: Both children and adults should eat around 500 grams of fruit and vegetables a day. In addition, legumes, such as beans and lentils, are recommended as a daily part of the diet.  Common mistake When it comes to getting children to eat more greens, persistence is often lacking. A common mistake is that parents give up too quickly. Introducing new flavors takes time – and requires patience. - It may not always go home the first time, but second, third, tenth. So have a little patience, says Karoline Pettersson, dietitian. She advises letting the children explore the food - feel, squeeze and taste at their own pace. You should preferably serve vegetables when the children are hungriest and not be afraid to mix fruit and vegetables. It's easy to just serve the classics, like carrot and cucumber, but there's not that much nutrition in cucumber. Five colors on the plate Instead of focusing only on the vegetables, Karoline Pettersson suggests that you talk about the colors on the plate and aim for five colors at every meal. Often a regular meal consists of about three colors – for example potatoes, meat or fish and a sauce. The challenge is to get it up to five, and let the extra colors come from vegetables. - There is usually a lot of nutrition in color. Another tip is to look for colors together with the children - and if they are old enough, take them to the store and make it a color hunt. That way, it will be easier to encourage vegetables. The dietitian also recommends making it more fun by varying how the vegetables are served. - Find slightly different ways to serve. It can be sticks or just presented in different bowls, says Karoline Pettersson.

Trafikverket: Salt is the working method At Trafikverket, they defend the method. Today, the emphasis is instead on accessibility and the requirement for good friction. - There is ongoing research and development, so it is possible that there is something else in the future. Bloody scrapes and broken bones are part of everyday life in ice racing. But according to the Swedish WC star, most accidents are relatively minor after all.

- It may not be seen so much on TV, but on the track it goes very fast. Especially when you drive four in one heat. Then it's tight and a lot of adrenaline, says Martin.

The sport is far from glamorous. Often it is family and friends who help behind the scenes.

- It's a good distraction, says Ari Haarahiltunen and laughs.  At the same time, he admits that the nervousness is always there.

- Before it was more exciting, then he was flying all the time. Almost every competition he was up in the snow embankment. One minute full discharge Martin began his career in motocross, but soon found a home in ice racing - a sport where a heat only lasts about a minute, but where everything is decided at a breakneck pace.

e2b60915a8c7296c3a562a749130ef6801215721: In Sweden, blood group A is most common, followed by 0, while 0 dominates in large parts of Africa – something that is believed to be connected with protection against severe malaria. The distribution of blood groups varies between different parts of the world and cannot be fully explained but appears to be influenced by historical disease and survival. - Assume that everyone has the same blood type and then a new type of infection comes that spreads in a population and everyone has the same blood type, so everyone dies, says Gustaf Edgren, medical researcher and associate professor of epidemiology. Blood group most important in transfusion People with blood group 0 are universal donors, while A, B and AB have more limited possibilities. The wrong blood type when transfused can be life-threatening, but it is very rare. The blood group is important for transfusions and for pregnant women in case of incompatibility, but otherwise has very little meaning in everyday life. - If you need a blood transfusion, healthcare always finds out your blood type, so you don't need to know it yourself, says Gustaf Edgren. Regardless of blood type, there may be concerns that the right blood is not available in the event of an accident or in healthcare. That's why it's important to donate blood if you can - more blood donors are always needed.  The doctor answers: the most common myths, Myth 1: A blood type protects against winter sickness - The answer is that there is. There is a blood group that is protective against winter sickness, says Gustaf Edgren and continues: - This is complicated, but there are lots of blood groups. And there is one that interacts with calici or the norovirus that causes winter sickness, which means that you have almost one hundred percent protection. Myth 2: Your blood type determines your personality - There is no evidence that this is the case, or any biological link. But this is a common myth. There are those who believe in it. There is a strange view of blood groups. People think magical things, says Edgren. Myth 3: It's important to adjust your diet based on your blood type - This is actually also false, but this is a really common myth. E

b75f7756cde6698291b46de819872dd831734aa2: Petter questioned by the police - about his children's book: "Not about sex"
9641042ce7aca18c984740965e14e652a43bb085: On Tuesday, the children's book author Petter Wallenberg was summoned for questioning by the police to answer questions about the hatred and threats generated by his children's book.  - It is great that the police are getting to the bottom of this, he says.  The book "Among dragons and drag queens" is based on modern interpretations of classic fairy tales. For nine years, the drag show theater company of the same name has toured Sweden and read the fairy tales to children, young people and adults. The performances have been praised, but Petter Wallenberg says that he has had to endure hatred and threats. - They have called us pedophiles, rapists, pigs and sick. Personally, I have been stalked, harassed and hanged. "It's bizarre" In the end, he chose to report the threats to the police and has since been interrogated continuously for several months. In the police interrogation, he has had it explained to him that those who report claim that they want to protect the children. - I have had to sit in police interrogations and explain: "No, the drag show is not about sex, and the book is not a sex story for children," says Petter Wallenberg.  In total, he has testified in eight trials and believes that he was met with prejudice and criticism even there. - It is bizarre that we have a court that seriously asks if there is any link between drag and pedophilia, and defense lawyers who say: "LGBTQ people really shouldn't be allowed to perform for children". Has led to convictions So far, Petter Wallenberg has made 200 reports against the hatred directed at him, which has led to 20 convictions for incitement against ethnic groups. Now he has submitted the book to the police so they can understand what the hate is directed at.  - It is good that the police are getting to the bottom of this, but I think it is the first children's book that becomes part of a police investigation. Now he hopes it will lead to change.  - More people must dare to report, the police must gain more knowledge and politicians must start acting.
7e6867819b874a83885ac15a23002a4972f414c1: The expert warns of Ica's advice: "You may die"
b66bb8e935990c585eaab9cf0f2a34389e94576c: In Ica's food magazine Buffé, readers are advised to make use of potato peels and leftover potato pieces by fermenting them with salt in a jar. The tip is highlighted as a simple hack that should give increased umami taste and serve as a tasty base for sauces. Now, however, the council is receiving sharp criticism from food hygiene professor Marie‑Louise Danielsson‑Tham. - The worst thing that can happen is that you die, she says. Deadly nerve agent Danielsson-Tham refers to the risk of the bacterium clostridium botulinum, which is found naturally in soil and can appear on potato skins. In the event of incorrect fermentation, the bacteria can form botulinum toxin, a life-threatening nerve agent. - Potato skins are almost impossible to clean. Small soil particles can carry spores that then develop into bacteria if the conditions are wrong, she says. The botulinum toxin lacks taste, smell and color, which means that a home cook cannot detect that the food has become dangerous. - You don't notice it until it's too late, says Danielsson‑Tham. "No heysan-hoppsan method" She emphasizes that fermentation is a complicated method that requires knowledge, the right raw materials and control over hygiene, amount of salt and pH value. - Fermenting is not a hello-hoppsan method. Perfect raw materials, the right amount of salt, thorough cleaning and a quick pH reduction are required for the process to be safe, she says. According to her, it is not possible to achieve the required level of hygiene if peels or defective potato residues are used. - It must be raw materials in absolute top condition. Leftover pieces or shells are not suitable, says Danielsson-Tham. Sees a lack of knowledge Marie-Louise Danielsson‑Tham has previously called for recipe creators and newspapers to seek the help of food hygiene expertise before publishing advice. - I see a risk with anyone who lacks sufficient knowledge. You should have a food hygienist read this sort of thing before it goes to print, she says. She describes how fermentation has become increasingly popular, not least linked to food waste and home preparation.

b37c5bc2f3661f730ae793d236450af050e2db20: It can be early signs of dementia: "Valuable clues"
003ce8cf9631f983878806af4f762038667030d1: Behavioral changes such as anxiety, depression, irritability, apathy or agitation can appear in older people long before a dementia diagnosis can be established. A new study conducted by researchers at the Karolinska Institute and the University of Perugia in Italy also shows that the symptoms can form patterns in both cognitively healthy and dementia-diagnosed people, which the site forskning.se was the first to report. 1,234 people aged 65 and over participated in the study. Four neuropsychiatric profiles were developed, with the lowest level showing no or very few symptoms and the strongest showing behavior dominated by delusions, agitation and irritability.  "Can give us valuable clues" Behavioral changes occurred in both groups, but were more pronounced in those diagnosed with dementia. 42 percent of the participants without dementia showed symptoms of any of the behavioral changes. According to the researchers, the results are important for understanding the development of dementia. "This can give us valuable clues about who is at higher risk of developing dementia. Our study also shows that certain clusters of symptoms occur together with treatable health conditions, which highlights opportunities for preventive strategies and earlier support," says Anna Marseglia, assistant lecturer at the department of neurobiology, care science and society at Karolinska Institutet who co-authored the study, in a press release. Will investigate connection to Alzheimer's The next step is to follow the participants over time to form an idea of ​​whether the neuropsychiatric profiles develop clinically and to investigate what role different factors play in the development. The researchers also plan to link the behavioral patterns of the people studied to blood-based biomarkers for Alzheimer's disease to better understand the underlying mechanisms that lead to dementia.

"Today I'm going to see Lilla Fridolf" Since both the name, address and phone number were on the letter, it wasn't that difficult to find the letter writer Per, who is 63 years old today. It was fantastic to be called, says Per.  But apart from war and misery, Per had also planned for the evening's entertainment. In addition to that, the Legislative Council sees several legal technical problems, including grading difficulties with what is a "penalty more severe than a fine". In its proposal, the government also takes aim at the role of prosecutors. For one thing, deportation will in future only be tried after a lawsuit from the prosecutor, something that the council approves. On the one hand, prosecutors must be obliged to request deportation when the crime is grounds for deportation, without making their own assessment as to whether the reasons for deportation are strong enough. Harsh criticism: "Stranger to the system" Just this has been met with harsh criticism from several heavy referral bodies, including the Public Prosecutor's Office. According to the authority, the proposal conflicts with the role of an independent legal authority and public trust risks being undermined when prosecutors are expected to act against better knowledge. The Council of Law considers that it is not "reasonable" to proceed with a proposal that has received so much criticism from experienced bodies and calls the proposal "system alien". "It is also indefensible both for efficiency reasons and out of consideration for all defendants who in the trial are to be threatened with deportation, even though it is clear to the person making the deportation request that deportation will not take place," writes the Legislative Council. The money comes partly from the EU's social climate fund, which accounts for 75 percent, and the rest is financed by the Swedish state. - The social climate fund aims to make the climate transition more fair, so that the households most affected by fuel prices will have the opportunity to participate in the transition, says Elin Hall, expert at the Environmental Protection Agency. Here are the criteria for the premium There are a number of criteria that must be met to receive the new electric car premium. It is about the premium going to households that need it the most and that are most affected by fuel prices. Firstly, you must live in a rural municipality or in an area that has limited access to public transport. The second is that the household's income must be below 80 percent of the average income in Sweden. - Household income means that we look at incomes for all adults in the household and then they are adjusted based on how many people the income should be enough for, says Elin Hall in Nyhetsmorgon. How much money you can get The most you can get is a total of SEK 64,800, divided into SEK 1,300 per month for a maximum of 36 months (SEK 46,800), plus a start-up grant of SEK 18,000. Around 800,000 households are deemed to meet the set criteria. You can get the premium for both new and used cars, but it can cost a maximum of SEK 450,000 - or if you choose to lease the car, it can cost SEK 4,600 a month. In addition, you must not have had an electric car or a plug-in hybrid in the last year. Do you notice the interest already? - I just received a report that some applications have already come in during the morning or night.

Caviar in a tube is a matter of course on many Swedish breakfast tables, but for the uninitiated the taste can be a challenge.

Broad test – big differences The panel assessed the taste, texture and appearance of Kalle's Kaviar Original, Svenne's mild smoke, Eldorado, Ejdern's original and Klädesholmen. Scores varied widely between participants, particularly for smokiness and saltiness. - After two everything tastes like caviar, stated Måns Möller, who nevertheless found a clear favourite. Tone Sekelius appreciated the caviar varieties that were balanced and had a nice color, while Marlene Eriksson preferred a clear rum flavor and classic saltiness. The panel agreed that accessories such as eggs can completely change the taste experience. Klädesholmen best in test When all points were added up, Klädesholmen was the winner, closely followed by Eldorado and Kalles. The exclusive Ejdern's original, with a high rum content, ended up in the middle of the results list. - I am positively surprised by Klädesholmen, which for me in any case is relatively new caviar. Kalles has always been the go-to, but maybe it will be new now, says Erik Videgård. The panel agreed that the test provided new insights into the Swedes' favorite toppings, and that the taste of caviar can surprise even the most devoted.

0d9d5cf73b2e1302293de5f174ebb9560fd20605:
Therese Lindén and Anna Sandberg lived ordinary lives. With work, family, plans ahead. Then came the news: grade 4 glioblastoma – one of the most aggressive and incurable brain tumors out there.

For Anna, it started with a headache and a fatigue that wouldn't let go. She thought it was a migraine. 
Therese, on the other hand, had almost no symptoms at all. A little headache, an Alvedon later, she rushed on in everyday life.

- For six months I was sure that they had sent it to the wrong patient. It wasn't on the world map that it was me, says Therese.

The diagnosis is hard to accept. When the news reached Anna, she sat quietly. - I said nothing. I just sat and yawned. It was as if my body reacted before I understood. Suddenly, everything changes. Working life is replaced by sick leave. Everyday life is filled with hospital visits, treatments and an uncertain future. At the same time, it is everyday life that keeps them both up. - I am grateful that weekdays roll by. That I can be with the children, cook and do ordinary things, says Anna. Support in each other They found each other through the illness. Today they share experiences, symptoms and the hardest part of all, living with a diagnosis that cannot be cured. - You don't need to explain. The other understands immediately, says Anna. But time is always present. It is no longer measured in years – but in months. The average for the disease is 15–18 months. Therese has passed 21. - Every month feels like a win. Every day too, she says.

Despite the dark prognosis, there is still hope. The hope for more time. About new treatments. About research that can change the future – for them and for others.

- You want to live on hope.

Above all, it involves two clear changes: The tightened amortization requirement of an additional 1 percentage point for loans that exceed 4.5 times per household's annual income is removed. At the same time, the mortgage ceiling is being raised from the current 85 to 90 percent. The effect of this is that buyers now need to put in a cash deposit corresponding to 10 percent of the home's value instead of the previous 15 percent.  What do you hope to achieve with these changes? For a first-time buyer, it is intended to make it easier as you do not need to have as much cash available. The fact that you also don't have to amortize as much should make it even easier. Overall, it is intended to provide more mobility throughout the housing chain.  In practical terms, what does the new amortization requirement mean financially? This of course depends on how large a loan you have as a mortgage holder. On a loan of two million kroner, a reduced amortization to 2 percent means a saving of kroner 1,667 per month. For the double loan amount, SEK 3,333.  It sounds good, where is the criticism against the change? On several points. Economists have warned that this will instead push up housing prices, especially for smaller apartments, precisely those that are relevant for first-time buyers.  A concern that is also raised by, among others, KI is that a higher mortgage ceiling will contribute to young people ending up with larger loans than assets if housing prices were to moderate or even fall.  Besides these two changes, are there other things to be aware of? Absolutely. The possibility of extending one's mortgage is limited. For those who want to take out an additional loan to renovate the kitchen or install a heat pump, the maximum loan-to-value ratio is lowered to 80 percent of the home's value.  What then happens if the apartment is revalued? With the new rules, you may only make a reassessment every five years. But in the summer it doesn't matter so much, because then it's so bright anyway.  Are more people dying in connection with the time change? No. There is an old classic Swedish study that showed that heart attacks went up by a few percent on the Monday and the Tuesday after. But now there was a big study that showed that it wasn't true. There are studies that showed slightly more accidents in traffic these days, but overall the risks are small. Is the switch to summer time more harmful than to winter time? Yes, you can say that, as you get reduced sleep. There is no risk in sleeping in for an hour more. For the vast majority it is a non-issue. Most people do this adjustment every weekend when they sleep longer and need to get up a little earlier on Monday. Just this weekend it will be a little extra difficult.  Can you catch up on the difference in sleep? Yes. Not everyone, but almost everyone falls asleep quickly. Our sleep is so dynamic and biologically strong that most people catch up on it in one night. Those who have a late rhythm will have a little more trouble adapting to society than they already have.   Is everyone equally affected by the time change? No, it's a huge difference. If you are outdoors a lot, you immediately change your mind, there are excellent studies that show that everyone who camps becomes morning people. Those who are out little, have longer rhythms and who tend to be evening people will have a little more trouble.

It was in 1989 that the couple, both from Storfors in Värmland, disappeared during a hiking trip on the Coromandel Peninsula on New Zealand's North Island. Admitted car theft Soon after the disappearance, Tamihere, who had been on the run from the police for three years in the Coromandel wilderness, became suspicious of unrelated crimes. It was when the couple's abandoned car was found that police were able to link it to him. David Tamihere admitted to stealing Höglin and Paakkonen's car, but said he never met them. Despite that, he was convicted of the murder. A verdict that was mostly based on circumstantial evidence, as their bodies had not been found. Body still missing Tamihere, who is now 72, has throughout denied the allegations. He was paroled in 2010, but has continued to fight to clear his name. Urban Höglin's body was found in 1991 by wild boar hunters. It was many kilometers away from the place it should have been, according to the prosecution's theories. Heidi Paakkonen's body is still missing. Witness convicted of perjury In 2024, the Court of Appeal ruled that the trial was not fair, due to an incorrect testimony in the district court by Roberto Conchie Harris, a man who was in the same holding cell as David Tamihere.  He claimed that Tamihere confessed to the murder to him, but was convicted in 2017 of perjury. Despite the fact that he lied, the Court of Appeal did not think there was enough reason to overturn the sentence against the man. The Supreme Court now judges that this was incorrect. On Tuesday, David Tamihere was cleared of murder, with the court admitting that a "fundamental error" had been made in sentencing him.

Of this, 16 kilos end up in the bin and 18 kilos in the sink.  That's why we throw away food The most common reason for throwing away food is that it feels stale or that you don't want to risk getting sick. Many take the safe side before the uncertain. - You may have forgotten the food in the fridge, you may have cooked too much food. You may not understand the date marking and that leads to feelings of worry and fear, says Karin Fritz, food waste expert at the Swedish Food Agency. Fruit and vegetables in particular are thrown away unnecessarily, often due to incorrect storage. Fritz believes that more knowledge is needed to reduce wastage. Tips for reducing food waste A simple way to reduce food waste is to lower the refrigerator temperature to four degrees - then the food can last up to twice as long compared to eight degrees. You must also use your senses to determine if the food is okay. - Only four out of ten Swedes know that food boxes can last up to a week in the fridge if the temperature is right, says Karin Fritz. To reduce waste, Fritz advises to take inventory of the fridge and freezer before purchasing, start from what is already at home and organize the fridge so that what needs to be eaten first is easily accessible. -  We really need to get better at it. It makes it easier for us in everyday life, says Karin Fritz.

3c446361f0528c6214710b68152a963d4ef083af: Chronic intestinal disease is increasing in children: "Very high numbers"
49e16a4b7c5c685b1e88c4450ccaf1933c6c3e12: Chronic intestinal inflammation is becoming more common worldwide. Inflammatory bowel diseases are more common in the Western world, but as countries industrialize and get better economies, the number of disease cases is increasing globally. - The theory is that it is something in the way we live and the food we eat that contributes to the disease, says Rana Eizad. What theories exist? Is it something we stuff into ourselves? - You can speculate on that. Genetics is a big part, we know that. Most likely it could be something we eat, the western diet that we have. The availability of medicines and antibiotics has been singled out as a culprit. Has almost quadrupled A new study in Denmark, where they looked at all children who have fallen ill from 1978 to 2020, shows that inflammatory bowel disease has increased sharply. If you go back to the period before 1990, there were four children per 100,000 annually who contracted these diseases, today the figure is 15 children per 100,000. - So there will be a threefold to fourfold increase. You might think that these are not such high numbers, should we make such a big deal about it? But it goes hand in hand with what we see globally. We have very high rates of inflammatory bowel disease in Sweden. One in a hundred Swedes is affected, says Rana Eizad. What the symptoms look like Inflammatory bowel diseases are autoimmune diseases where the immune system attacks its own intestine. Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis are included in the group. The symptoms are stomach pain, loose stools, diarrhea, bloody stools and involuntary weight loss. Many of the symptoms are similar in people with IBS, but not blood in the stool. It is a sign of chronic intestinal inflammation. When should you seek care? - If you have blood in your stool, you should seek medical attention. It's usually hemorrhoids or intestinal pouches, but you shouldn't speculate on that. You have to get it investigated, says Rana Eizad.

It is built of wood from the royal ship Riksäppelt, launched in 1662 and sunk off Dalarö in 1676.
Jim Herlin found the wood via a homestead in Söderköping. - We moved the holiday package and pushed beams into the car, he says. The 400-year-old wood now lives on in both the fingerboard and neck in the middle of rock history. From silence to stage Once the guitar was sent on its way, there was silence. No answer. Then – suddenly – it appeared. In the hands of Keith Richards.

On stage. In front of an audience. - It was like a gift from above, says Jim Herlin. 400-year-old wood that still rocks Today, Jim Herlin continues to build guitars in his workshop in Saltsjöbaden. But the material makes demands. - The body had to be impregnated with superglue to hold it together. It's the mask, he says. The result is an instrument with a history spanning four centuries – from the bottom of the sea to the world's biggest stages.

In the past, it has been shown that it can protect against certain bacteria. Now it turns out that the peptide can have an important role in how we cope with the flu virus. A research group from Spain has analyzed samples from 19 people who work in health care and who state that they have never had the flu. The analyzes showed that they had a high concentration of dermcidin, which could be an explanation for their not being infected.  Lab studies The researchers also did lab studies where they saw that dermcidin could prevent two common flu viruses from attaching to human cells. The peptide also protected mice from contracting the flu. The study has been published in the scientific journal Pnas. "The results show that our own bodies have natural mechanisms to prevent viral infections, which opens up opportunities to develop new, more effective antiviral treatments," says Álex Mira, researcher at the Fisabio Foundation and one of the researchers behind the study, in a press release.

Then they are sometimes struck by exhaustion and extreme fatigue, outbursts and meltdowns, says Johanna Goa, behavioral scientist and therapist. "Especially common in girls" Goa also says that children with ADHD can keep it together for a whole school day, but when they get home they explode.  - It is very common, especially in girls. I tend to think that it's like shaking a Coke bottle. For every thing that is hard at school that actually takes a lot of effort but that may not be so clearly visible on the outside, this Coke bottle is shaken.  Then when you get home, it's like the lid off and explosion. - But it is also very important for the school to understand that this is what it looks like very often, says Johanna Goa. Difficulty directing focus - not concentration Another misconception is that people with ADHD cannot concentrate on anything. - You can do that very often, but you find it very difficult to direct your focus on what you should perhaps be focusing on. Combined diagnoses confuse Adhd is also something that is congenital.  - It has nothing to do with upbringing. If you have a combination of diagnoses, such as ADHD and autism, the symptoms can be confusing. - When you have both, it often becomes something completely different. Many times this adhd side may want stimulation and increased challenges, but then the autism may not really be able to handle that and is very easily overstimulated.

The women who lived in Kallinge all five years before giving birth are counted in the study as exposed to very high PFAS exposure. Basically, according to the Minister of Justice, it is about the fact that it is not the experts, for example in the Legislative Council, who decide. Politicians do that.

- What is a fair punishment is difficult to research. We believe that it is reasonable that the citizens' elected representatives in the Riksdag must weigh in on that issue, and therefore we are proceeding with reforms that we think have good reasons for them, says the prime minister.

You implement the will of the people, you mean?

- Yes, we do so to the extent that this is a change in policy, a tightening of the punishment that has been discussed for a long time in politics, some would say several decades, which has also received broad support in general elections among citizens. The Law Council: A "hasty act" Regarding the penal reform, which will increase the punishment for about fifty crimes, the Law Council believes that it is a "hasty act" that is of "lack of quality". The content is, according to the authority, that the changes to the law should not be implemented.

Gunnar Strömmer believes that it is a political issue that the Legislative Council has decided on - namely whether the penalty should be increased or not.

- I am not of the opinion that you should prevent the Legislative Council from submitting opinions, but depending on the nature of the opinions, you can say that politics has more or less room to take them into account or make its own considerations.

Something that they mean in the long run could threaten the food supply in the whole of Europe. - Now there is an influx of extremely cheap, fake honey from above all China. Colder waters in the Atlantic At the same time that El Niño hits parts of the world hard, there are others who benefit. 60745e6602ea79d16858676cf4ba3f3be58f9f55: 800,000 tons of carbon dioxide are captured and buried under the seabed
467016f25263c18893613e8d610658cb6743f722:
The technology is called bio-CCS and means that the carbon dioxide from the combustion of biofuels in the Värtaverket is captured - something that in practice produces negative emissions. And on the night of Saturday, a crucial pipe was put in place – from the facility down to the port.

- Here we are building a new quay where boats will add and load carbon dioxide before it is transported on to Norway, says Tobias Pelicano, deputy director for bio-CCS at Stockholm Exergi. Several million tons from different countries are to be buried. The plan is for everything to be ready in 2028. At that time, approximately 800,000 tons of carbon dioxide per year will be shipped away from the Värtaverket. But Stockholm is not first.

Already today, around 400,000 tonnes of carbon dioxide is transported per year from a cement factory in Brevik in Norway. And several other European facilities are on their way into the system – including in the Netherlands and Denmark.

In total, up to three million tons of carbon dioxide per year can be collected and sent to a transshipment terminal outside Bergen before the end of the decade. 100 kilometers out – and 2,600 meters down From the terminal, the carbon dioxide is pumped further into pipes on the seabed. 100 kilometers out into the North Sea, it is pushed down 2,600 meters below the seabed. There it is stored in a water-filled sandstone formation.

- The carbon dioxide is dissolved in the water and stored in a geological formation permanently, says Fridtjof Wisur, who is the commercial director of Northern Lights. "We are absolutely sure" He is convinced that the carbon dioxide will not leak out.

- Yes, we are absolutely sure. We monitor both the plant and the storage continuously to ensure that the carbon dioxide stays where it should, says Fridtjof Wisur. - It's simple. You don't have to declare. It's a simple way to do taxes, says Christina Sahlberg, savings economist at Skandia.

An investment savings account is a so-called standard taxed account. This means that you don't have to pay tax every time you sell your assets at a profit, unlike a regular mutual fund account. You pay a certain percentage of tax per year based on the value of your account. Since January 2026, the first SEK 300,000 on an ISK is also completely tax-free. This is a doubling compared to 2025, when the free amount was SEK 150,000 Important advice Child savings are increasing but there are pitfalls
Today, roughly 211,000 children under the age of 16 have their own investment savings account. Here are a few things to keep in mind.

- You can either have an ISK that you open in your own name and save for your children. Then you have full control over this money and can give it to your children at any time. Or you can open an ISK in the children's name. Then you get to take advantage of this tax exemption, because it applies per person. But then it is very important to remember that it is legally the children's money, explains Christina Sahlberg.

At the lab, the meat from all wild boars shot in the Gävle region must be measured. The guideline value in Sweden is 1,500 becquerels per kilogram. But only about a quarter of the pigs are approved. Ulf Frykman, at CJ Analys, who has measured radioactive levels in venison for 39 years, believes that it is far too much. - If you follow the Swedish Food Agency's recommendations, you can eat meat with 3,000 becquerels once in a while. But 10,000 should never be eaten. And we have many that are over 10,000, he says. The pig stirs up the cesium in the ground Janne and Jörgen Linander, father and son, often hunt wild boar together. They point out burrow tracks in the ground and tell us that the pigs are often looking for grubs, worms and roots, a bit down in the soil layer. - Then they unfortunately stir up the ground-based cesium that has fallen over these years, says Jörgen Linander. As chairman of the Gävle southern game management circle, he is the one who calls on the hunters to submit samples of the meat.

- We have told the hunters to measure every single pig. In this district, the values ​​are so high, so you don't get careless, says Jörgen Linander. 40 percent of the radioactivity remains 40 years ago, Jörgen was only a couple of years old and his mother has told us that he was playing outside when the radioactive rain fell. - I haven't had cancer yet, but you have to keep an eye on it. You never know if it can have an impact, he says. The half-life of cesium 137 is 30 years. This means that approximately 40 percent of the original radioactivity still remains. - It hasn't disappeared yet. It is here on the hill below us, says Janne Linander.

Republican Senator Tom Tillis has announced that he will vote no on Warsh until the issue of the investigation against Powell is resolved, effectively blocking the nomination.

Start with a smaller boat Patrik Östberg, chairman of the boat club, looks forward to the start of the season and reminds us of the importance of planning your finances when buying a boat. - When you make a budget, you should add 20 percent, because it is always more expensive with insurance, oils and the means you need to keep the boat in shape. Early mobile debut Today, 90 percent of Swedish 10-year-olds and 95 percent of 11-year-olds have a smart phone. We look with concern at a development where children have gone from a play-based childhood to a smartphone-based childhood. You have a note machine that is constantly switched on, he says. It affects sleep and mental health, and Swedish children are particularly affected, according to the minister. We like to be modern and this has also led to us giving children smartphones very early in Sweden. We also now have the most sedentary children in the Nordics. A smartphone is also worse than a tablet or computer because it is constantly present, according to Forssmed. Researchers with whom he has been in contact point out that there are reasons to postpone the age of the telephone premiere. He himself does not want to say what age would be suitable, but still gives a hint. I can state for myself that the researchers I talk to about this, then it's about 13-14 years. To be presented this summer He also points to Denmark and Finland, where various authorities sat for 13 years as a guideline. An age limit can be presented as early as June 30 this year when the investigation is partially reported and then the Public Health Agency must disseminate the information to the public. It can be of great help to parents, according to Forssmed. Then those who want to introduce a smartphone earlier get to justify it, rather than parents who want to wait trying to justify it to their children or to other parents, says Forssmed.
